Subject: APAC standby activation — RTO/RPO request and SLA redline

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, NovaBank's regulator requires that our primary production region in APAC be protected by a documented standby activation plan. Because of our data residency and certification constraints we cannot move to an active-active architecture right now.

We're asking Redwood to accept an APAC-specific carveout in the SLA: standby activation (warm standby) with an RTO of 2 hours and RPO of 60 minutes for the APAC region only. This is longer than Redwood's standard geo-failover commitments, but it maps to what our auditors will accept.

I've attached a redline of the SLA (SLA_redline_v3.pdf) and a sketch from our cloud partner showing the proposed warm-standby topology. We are under a procurement deadline: we need an agreed position and a contract with redlines accepted by 2029-09-12 to meet quarter-end signoff.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to (a) accept the APAC-specific RTO/RPO window as an exception, (b) enumerate any additional operational requirements (DR test cadence, runbook standards, post-failover verification), and (c) confirm any incremental standby premium or operational fee?

Appreciate a short summary by EOD Thursday 2029-09-05 if possible so our procurement/legal can proceed.

Thanks,
Priya Menon

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: NovaBank APAC RTO/RPO exception — ops assessment

Karthik / Soojin —

Quick operational assessment: a 2-hour RTO + 60-minute RPO is achievable with warm-standby but with conditions:
- Data replication: we need a sub-5-minute snapshot/replication window for critical datasets or a streaming replication pipeline. If NovaBank has batch-only replication at hourly granularity, we'll need to shift to near-real-time replication (change-data-capture).
- KV cache & model state: for inference workloads, cold caches materially increase request tail latency after failover. We recommend a pre-warmed cache snapshot and a prioritized prefilling process triggered during declared incidents.
- Capacity reservation: to guarantee RTO, Redwood must reserve a warm pool of instances in APAC that can be flipped into active mode without queuing. That is the primary driver of the standby premium.
- Test cadence: quarterly DR drills, with the first run within 30 days post-contract, including runbook sign-off and RPO verification via synthetic traffic.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: large CRDB restores could exceed 2 hours for very large volumes. Mitigation: agree SLOs per dataset or require tiering of datasets that need the 60m RPO.
- Risk: cross-region network outages that block replication. Mitigation: dual-path replication (primary ↔ inter-region relay) and documented failover fallbacks.

I've attached a short topology sketch (apac-standby-architecture.png) showing the recommended arrangements (replication, warm pools, prefilling). If NovaBank can confirm streaming replication for critical tables and accept the standby premium, ops can support the exception in the addendum.

— Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Priya — thanks for the patience while we reviewed this with ops and commercial. Below is a concise proposal for NovaBank to move forward fast:

1) Redwood position (proposed exception)
- APAC-only SLA addendum: RTO = up to 2 hours, RPO = up to 60 minutes for agreed critical datasets. This will be recorded as a formal exception to the global SLA and appended as an addendum to the MSA.

2) Operational requirements (must be satisfied prior to signing)
- Streaming replication (CDC) in place for critical datasets or sub-5-minute snapshot replication for any dataset covered by the exception.
- Accept quarterly DR drills; first drill to occur within 30 days post-signature.
- Runbook and playbook acceptance: NovaBank to share runbooks; Redwood will perform runbook review and sign-off.
- Pre-approved capacity reservation: standby warm pool reserved in APAC sized at agreed baseline (to be costed).

3) Commercials
- Standby premium: estimated 20% uplift on the committed capacity for the region (final percent subject to committed baseline). Karthik will share a term sheet and final pricing by tomorrow.

4) Next steps & timeline
- If this is acceptable, we will:
  a) Circulate a one-page addendum (Lauren will draft)
  b) Confirm standby pool sizing and pricing (Karthik)
  c) Schedule an ops handoff and preliminary runbook review (Jonas)
  d) Circulate DocuSign link for signature (planned target: 2029-09-10)

DocuSign link (draft): https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/NOVA-EXC-2029
Runbook share: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/runbooks/novabank-apac-dr

If you confirm, we will convert the SLA_redline_v3.pdf to an internal-redline + addendum and move to DocuSign.
